summary: Studio Gang's 23-story, 254-unit rental tower at 1070 Bridgeview Way, the fourth and last Phase 1 building. Construction started March 2022, leasing began April 2024, residents moved in from June 2024 and the ribbon was cut September 3, 2024; 59 of its units are below market rate after a 2024 re-mix toward 90% AMI. Chipotle's own location page for 365 Toni Stone Xing, Unit C gives an opening date of September 23, 2026 (a date stated by the business, on a page captured the next day).

milestones.text: Port Commission adopts Resolutions 18-03 to 18-10, approving the Mission Rock DDA, Design Controls and related documents

Board of Supervisors affirms the Planning Commission's EIR certification (the Port's October 2023 memo gives Resolution 33-18; the Notice of Determination gives File No. 171286); Notice of Determination filed March 9, 2018
Development Agreement and Disposition and Development Agreement take effect (DA term 30 years)

The developer's Phase 1 Phase Submittal proposes swapping Parcel F into Phase 1 in place of Parcel K, adding roughly 100 units (about 40 affordable) and a four-sided intersection instead of a linear street alignment. The Port's resolution says the Phase Submittal with this boundary change was submitted on April 4, 2019; the developer's Phase 1 overview (a document dated July 2, 2019) says the submittal was submitted on December 4, 2018 and revised on April 24, 2019, and describes the swap in the past tense without dating it
Port Commission approves the Phase 1 budget with Parcel F in the phase (Resolution 19-39)
Port executes the 75-year prepaid Parcel F lease (Lease No. L-16706) with Mission Rock Parcel F Owner, L.L.C.; memorandum recorded October 7, 2020

Commercial Property Executive (article dated July 14, 2026) is the only source for a $116.2M construction loan from Wells Fargo originated in 2022; the article could not be read when this record was checked (HTTP 403), so the amount, lender and year are unconfirmed

Construction starts (the Port says it started in March 2022 'due to the unique financial structure of the project, including the payment of Jobs Housing Equivalency Fees by the office projects to subsidize the below-market rate housing')
The Port's October 6, 2023 memo reports Building F's structural elements as topped out (the topping-out date itself is not given)
Port Commission (Resolution 24-21) approves re-mixing Parcel F's BMR units from 97 (38%) to 59 (23%): 35 at 90% AMI, 24 at 120% AMI, none at 150%
Leasing launch announced (SF YIMBY: two days before the April 25, 2024 China Basin Park opening next door)

Residents begin moving in (SF YIMBY, September 4, 2024: "the building has been open to new residents since June"; the Port's April 2024 memo had forecast move-ins in June 2024, and its March 2025 memo says "As of February 2025, seven months into lease-up", which would put lease-up from about July 2024)
Ribbon cutting with Mayor London Breed; about 20% of units leased at that point
Leasing status: 36 of 59 BMR units (61%) and 98 of 195 market-rate units (50%) leased

Commercial Property Executive (article dated July 14, 2026) is the only source for a $117.8M loan from Ares Management, described there as refinancing the earlier construction loan; the article could not be read when this record was checked (HTTP 403), so the amount, lender and what it replaced are unconfirmed, and the month shown is the article's publication month, not a closing date
DBI site permit 201910073784 for new construction of Building F (23 stories, 258 residential units with retail, office, restaurant and assembly) approved; filed October 7, 2019
DBI permit 202312293282, a revision/architectural+MEP addendum for Mission Rock Building F (revision to PA #201910073784 S3 and Port application B-2022-0127), is approved

open_questions: Commercial Property Executive's July 14, 2026 article (the only source for the $116.2 million Wells Fargo construction loan and the $117.8 million Ares Management loan) returned HTTP 403 on 2026-10-12, and a second page listed in a web search for the same loan (traded.co) did too, so neither amount, lender nor what the Ares loan replaced is confirmed by a page read here.

Jobs Housing Equivalency Fee subsidy received by Parcel F: the Port's September 2019 budget report lists a minimum of 75.6 ($ millions) for Parcel F when it was planned with 106 below-market units (it has 59), and says the residential projects "will request a proportionate share of the JHEF when the residential building foundations have been completed"; no source read gives the amount actually paid to Parcel F.

Construction cost: no source read states one. DBI permit 201910073784 carries a $99,907,840 estimated and revised cost, which is a filed permit valuation rather than a cost, and the only financing figure is the reported $116.2 million Wells Fargo loan, which is unconfirmed (see the first question).

Exact TCO date: the Port's October 2023 memo projected a June 2024 TCO, and its April 2024 memo said Parcel F "is expected to receive a Temporary Certificate of Occupancy (TCO) in May" with move-ins in June 2024 (both are projections); no document read gives the date the TCO was issued.
Topping-out date: the Port's October 2023 memo only says it had topped out; no dated press item found.

Total square footage disagrees across sources (287,000 / 314,508 / 315,000 / 330,000: a trade-press article reposted by Mitsui Fudosan America, the Port's 2019 appraisal table, the 2026 refinancing report, and SF YIMBY in March 2022); no document read says which is the gross floor area, and the DBI permit records read carry no floor area.

Images: no 'before' photo is hosted (until 2020 the parcel was the Seawall Lot 337 surface parking lot) and no rendering is hosted because the architects' renderings are not openly licensed; they are reachable through the architect sources listed here.

A Mapillary storefront photo of Ike's Love & Sandwiches (a sourced retail tenant, see the retail fact above) was hosted briefly and then removed: on review it read as too cluttered (a trash bin, a parked car and several pedestrians in front of the sign) to keep. Still on the shot list for a cleaner frame.
Arsicault Bakery's Verde shop is shown open on a March 11, 2025 release; it has not been re-confirmed since.

A business registration for BVNK at 365 Toni Stone Xing Fl 3 exists since 2025-03-30 (System Pay Services (Us), Inc., no end date, DataSF Registered Business Locations); no source read shows an office open there, so BVNK is not listed as a tenant. Searches found no page that names BVNK at Mission Rock.

Chipotle Mexican Grill is shown open from 2026-09-23. That date is the 'c_openDate' on Chipotle's own location page for 365 Toni Stone Xing (locations.chipotle.com, whose data carries a timestamp of 2026-09-24 and which was read on 2026-10-12); it is a date the company states, not one confirmed by a news report or a visit. The page lists daily hours of 10:45 a.m. to 10 p.m. and online ordering. DataSF has a registration for Chipotle Mexican Grill #5956 at suite C from 2026-08-25, which is a registration date, not an opening date.

First move-in month: SF YIMBY (September 4, 2024) says the building "has been open to new residents since June", while the Port's March 2025 memo says "As of February 2025, seven months into lease-up", which would put the start of lease-up around July 2024. No certificate of occupancy or lease document read dates the first move-in, so "June 2024" is approximate.

Resolution number for the Board of Supervisors' March 6, 2018 action: the Port's October 2023 memo gives Resolution 33-18 for the Board's affirmation of the EIR certification, but the same memo (and the Port's September 2019 and April 2024 reports) also cites Resolution 33-18 for the Board's February 2018 approval of the Development Agreement (with Resolution 42-18 for the DDA); the Notice of Determination gives only File No. 171286.
